questions.question_text: For two events $A$ and $B$, $P(A) = 0.25$, $P(B) = 0.60$, and $P(A \cap B) = 0.15$. Which statement is correct?

options.text: $A$ and $B$ are independent because $P(A) \times P(B) = 0.15 = P(A \cap B)$.
$A$ and $B$ are dependent because $P(A \cap B) \neq P(A) + P(B)$.
options.why: Applied the addition rule instead of the multiplication test for independence.

options.text: $A$ and $B$ are dependent because $P(A) \neq P(B)$.
options.why: Confused independence of events with events having equal probabilities.

options.text: $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive because $P(A \cap B) > 0$.
options.why: Confused independence with mutual exclusivity, which requires $P(A \cap B) = 0$.

questions.solution_text:
$P(A) \times P(B) = 0.25 \times 0.60$
$= 0.15$
Since $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B) = 0.15$, $A$ and $B$ are independent.

questions.question_text: For two events $X$ and $Y$, $P(X) = \frac{3}{8}$, $P(Y) = \frac{4}{9}$, and $P(X \cap Y) = \frac{1}{6}$. Test whether $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

options.text: Independent, because $P(X) \times P(Y) = \frac{1}{6} = P(X \cap Y)$.
Dependent, because $\frac{3}{8} \neq \frac{4}{9}$.
options.why: Compared $P(X)$ directly with $P(Y)$ instead of checking $P(X \cap Y) = P(X)P(Y)$.

options.text: Dependent, because $\frac{3}{8} + \frac{4}{9} \neq \frac{1}{6}$.
options.why: Added the probabilities instead of multiplying them.

options.text: Mutually exclusive, because $P(X \cap Y) = \frac{1}{6}$.
options.why: Claimed non-zero intersection implies mutual exclusivity.

questions.solution_text:
$P(X) \times P(Y) = \frac{3}{8} \times \frac{4}{9}$
$= \frac{12}{72}$
$= \frac{1}{6}$
Since $P(X \cap Y) = P(X) \times P(Y) = \frac{1}{6}$, $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

questions.question_text: For two events $J$ and $K$, $P(J) = 0.40$, $P(K) = 0.50$, and $P(J \mid K) = 0.40$. Which statement is true?

options.text: $J$ and $K$ are independent because $P(J \mid K) = P(J)$.
$J$ and $K$ are dependent because $P(J \mid K) \neq P(K)$.
options.why: Compared $P(J \mid K)$ to $P(K)$ instead of comparing to $P(J)$.

options.text: $J$ and $K$ are mutually exclusive because $P(J \mid K) = 0.40$.
options.why: Confused conditional probability with mutual exclusivity.

options.text: $J$ and $K$ cannot be tested without knowing $P(J \cap K)$.
options.why: Did not recognize that $P(J \mid K) = P(J)$ is a sufficient test for independence.

questions.solution_text:
The condition for independence is $P(J \mid K) = P(J)$.
Since $P(J \mid K) = 0.40 = P(J)$, knowing that $K$ occurred has no effect on the probability of $J$.
Therefore, $J$ and $K$ are independent.

questions.question_text:
The table shows $50$ gym members classified by age and membership type.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c} & \text{Full} & \text{Off-peak} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Under 30} & 15 & 10 & 25 \\ \text{30 and over} & 15 & 10 & 25 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 30 & 20 & 50 \end{array}$
Is having a Full membership ($F$) independent of being Under 30 ($U$)?

options.text: Yes, because $P(U \cap F) = 0.30$ and $P(U) \times P(F) = 0.30$.
No, because $15$ members are both Under 30 and have a Full membership.
options.why: Believed that having non-zero overlap prevents independence.

options.text: No, because there are more Full members than Off-peak members.
options.why: Judged independence based on row totals rather than the product test.

options.text: Yes, because $P(U) = P(\text{30 and over}) = 0.50$.
options.why: Confused equal group sizes with independence of the two variables.

questions.solution_text:
$P(U) = \frac{25}{50} = 0.50$
$P(F) = \frac{30}{50} = 0.60$
$P(U \cap F) = \frac{15}{50} = 0.30$
$P(U) \times P(F) = 0.50 \times 0.60$
$= 0.30$
Since $P(U \cap F) = P(U) \times P(F) = 0.30$, having a Full membership and being Under 30 are independent.

questions.question_text:
The table shows $120$ vehicles in a car park.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c} & \text{Electric} & \text{Petrol} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Sedan} & 18 & 42 & 60 \\ \text{SUV} & 12 & 48 & 60 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 30 & 90 & 120 \end{array}$
Test whether being Electric ($E$) and being a Sedan ($S$) are independent.

options.text: Dependent, because $P(E \cap S) = 0.15$ while $P(E) \times P(S) = 0.125$.
Independent, because $P(E \cap S) = \frac{18}{120} > 0$.
options.why: Assumed any non-zero joint probability implies independence.

options.text: Independent, because Sedan and SUV have the same row total of $60$.
options.why: Confused equal category marginals with variable independence.

options.text: Dependent, because $P(E) = 0.25 \neq 0.50 = P(S)$.
options.why: Compared marginal probabilities to each other instead of testing $P(E \cap S) = P(E)P(S)$.

questions.solution_text:
$P(E) = \frac{30}{120} = 0.25$
$P(S) = \frac{60}{120} = 0.50$
$P(E \cap S) = \frac{18}{120} = 0.15$
$P(E) \times P(S) = 0.25 \times 0.50$
$= 0.125$
Since $P(E \cap S) = 0.15 \neq 0.125 = P(E) \times P(S)$, $E$ and $S$ are dependent.

questions.question_text: In a Venn diagram with $40$ outcomes, $n(A \text{ only}) = 12$, $n(A \cap B) = 8$, $n(B \text{ only}) = 12$, and $n((A \cup B)') = 8$. Are $A$ and $B$ independent?

options.text: Dependent, because $P(A \cap B) = 0.20$ while $P(A) \times P(B) = 0.25$.
Independent, because $n(A \text{ only}) = n(B \text{ only}) = 12$.
options.why: Confused symmetry in unique elements with statistical independence.

options.text: Independent, because $P(A) = 0.50$ and $P(B) = 0.50$.
options.why: Assumed equal marginal probabilities guarantee independence.

options.text: Mutually exclusive, because $A$ and $B$ overlap in $8$ elements.
options.why: Contradicted the definition of mutually exclusive, which requires $n(A \cap B) = 0$.

questions.question_text: Two events $A$ and $B$ are independent, with $P(A) = 0.2$ and $P(A \cup B) = 0.56$. Find $P(B)$.

options.why: Subtracted $P(A)$ from $P(A \cup B)$ without accounting for the intersection term $P(A \cap B)$.
Divided $P(A \cup B)$ by $1 - P(A) = 0.8$ without subtracting $P(A)$ from the numerator.
Added $P(A)$ to $P(A \cup B)$ instead of setting up the addition formula to solve for $P(B)$.

questions.solution_text:
$P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$
Since $A$ and $B$ are independent, $P(A \cap B) = 0.2 P(B)$.
$0.56 = 0.2 + P(B) - 0.2 P(B)$
$0.36 = 0.8 P(B)$
$P(B) = \frac{0.36}{0.8}$
$= 0.45$

questions.question_text: Events $A$ and $B$ are independent. In a Venn diagram, $P(A) = 0.5$ and $P(A' \cap B) = 0.3$. Find $P(A \cap B)$.

options.why: Multiplied $P(A) = 0.5$ by $0.3$ directly without finding $P(B)$ first.
Subtracted $0.3$ from $P(A) = 0.5$ instead of solving for $P(B)$.
Found $P(B)$ correctly but did not multiply by $P(A)$ to get $P(A \cap B)$.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between mutually exclusive events and independent events for two events $A$ and $B$ with $P(A) > 0$ and $P(B) > 0$?

options.text: If $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, they cannot be independent because $P(A \cap B) = 0 \neq P(A) \times P(B)$.
Mutually exclusive events are always independent because they do not affect each other.
options.why: Confused having no outcomes in common with having no statistical dependence.

options.text: If $A$ and $B$ are independent, they must also be mutually exclusive.
options.why: Incorrectly claimed independence implies empty intersection.

options.text: Mutually exclusive and independent mean the same thing in probability.
options.why: Confused the two distinct mathematical concepts.

questions.solution_text:
Mutually exclusive events have $P(A \cap B) = 0$.
For independent events, $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B)$.
Since $P(A) > 0$ and $P(B) > 0$, the product $P(A) \times P(B) > 0$, so $P(A \cap B) = 0 \neq P(A) \times P(B)$.
Therefore, mutually exclusive events with non-zero probabilities can never be independent.

questions.question_text: Two events $A$ and $B$ are independent. $P(A) = x$, $P(B) = 2x$, and $P(A \cup B) = 0.72$. Find the value of $x$.

options.why: Solved $3x = 0.72$ without subtracting the intersection term $P(A \cap B) = 2x^2$.
Found $P(B) = 2x$ instead of $x = P(A)$.
Took the larger algebraic root of the quadratic equation which exceeds 1.

questions.solution_text:
$P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$
Since $A$ and $B$ are independent, $P(A \cap B) = x(2x) = 2x^2$.
$0.72 = x + 2x - 2x^2$
$2x^2 - 3x + 0.72 = 0$
$50x^2 - 75x + 18 = 0$
$(2x - 1)(25x - 18) = 0 \implies x = 0.3 \text{ or } x = 1.2$
Since $P(B) = 2x \le 1$, we must have $x \le 0.5$.
$x = 0.3$
